result.title: Odor + shock gives a T-maze memory (Tully & Quinn 1985)
result.citation: Tully T, Quinn WG (1985) Classical conditioning and retention in normal and mutant Drosophila melanogaster. Journal of Comparative Physiology A 157:263-277
result.read: abstract only (Europe PMC record of PubMed 3939242); the full text was not read

questions.prompt: You train a fly with odor A + shock (six cycles) and odor B without. At the choice point, what is its performance index (1 = always picks the odor that was not shocked)? And an unpaired control, with the same odors and shocks never together?

verdict.basis: effect size and direction only: n = 4 is too few flies for the validation's p < 0.01 (the smallest one-sided Wilcoxon p at n = 4 is 0.0625)

questions.note: The game's learning rule on the connectome's own Kenyon-cell to output-neuron synapses gives odor-specific memory. The sim's PI is higher than real flies' (the paper's 95% avoiding is a PI of about 0.9 if every fly did it): it was not tuned to match.

comparison.your_hypothesis: no difference between paired and unpaired
comparison.paper_direction: paired flies avoid the shocked odor (PI of 0.5 or more); unpaired flies don't
